## Overview

This case study evaluated the energy and water performance of Ellison Hall, a high-occupancy academic building at UCSB originally built in 1969. Despite earning LEED Gold certification, Ellison Hall revealed ongoing inefficiencies, particularly in water use, that could be addressed with cost-effective retrofits. The assessment focused on ENERGY STAR benchmarking, indoor water use analysis, and simple upgrades such as aerators, urinals, and lighting sensors. The final version proposed both low-cost and capital-intensive improvements to further align the building with UCSB’s climate action goals.
